_comment: The agent harness configuration. ONE file, two readers (config.ps1 for the
scripts, config.py for the Mattermost bridge), so a value is never defined
twice in two languages. Precedence, resolved only in the loaders:
built-in defaults < this file < harness.local.json (gitignored) < environment
This file is committed and MUST NOT contain secrets - it holds policy and
topology only. Machine-specific or experimental overrides go in
harness.local.json beside it.

extension._why_locked: operator 2026-08-28: the surface the operator drives interactively must never silently degrade to a weaker model.

mattermost._note: switchable in a thread with 'profile: <name>', the same shape as the existing 'model:' and 'worktree:' directives.

claude-code._note: a Claude Code agent - a subagent in an editor session, or 'claude -p' spawned by the bridge. Model names are CLI aliases, not API ids.

_why_container_workspace: The daemon's workspace root INSIDE the container (little-coder.config.yaml's
workspace.path), which is also the agent's cwd for every task. The quadrant
comparison mirrors a run workspace into this directory and mirrors the changed
files back out, because little-coder's workspace is a docker VOLUME shared with
open-terminal - there is no bind mount from a host worktree into the container, and
the daemon's own focus path clones from a git-host URL only (urlnorm.py rejects
local paths and file://). Declared here rather than assumed in code so a config
change is the whole change if the daemon's workspace ever moves.
little-coder._note: the local substrate: little-coder reaches llama-cpp through LiteLLM. Dispatched by dispatch.ps1 (Invoke-HarnessTask).
_why_lease: Focusing this runner WIPES its workspace and a task runs arbitrary commands in it,
so a dispatch is a live-plane mutation. dispatch.ps1's Assert-RunnerLease refuses
unless the named lease is held BY THE CALLER (lease.ps1 -Acquire -Name coder).
A runner without this key needs no lease - the policy lives here, not in the code.
Added 2026-08-30: the code claimed 'callers take the coder lease' in a comment while
nothing acquired, asserted or checked one.
_why_docker_exec: This runner declared endpoint 'http://127.0.0.1:8090' until 2026-08-30. That door did
so `curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/health` from the host is connection-refused while
`docker exec little-coder curl http://localhost:8090/health` answers. Nothing called
it, so nothing noticed. base_url is therefore CONTAINER-LOCAL and only meaningful
DECLARES, not publishes: not even 9091 exists on the running container - `docker port`
prints nothing and .NetworkSettings.Ports is {"9090/tcp":[]}. That disagreement is
measured; its CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. See MODULE.md's DECLARED-is-not-EXISTS note.
The port stays unpublished deliberately: daemon.py's own header says 'It is NOT the
task-trigger authentication surface; that is lc-mcpo', and lc-mcpo was retired
2026-08-20 - so POST /tasks (arbitrary agent execution) and POST /admin/shutdown are
unauthenticated. Reaching them through `docker exec` needs Docker access, which is
already an admin-equivalent boundary; publishing them on the host loopback would hand
them to every process on the machine for no capability the harness needs.
REVERT: set transport to 'http', base_url to 'http://127.0.0.1:8090', and add
dispatch.ps1's Invoke-LcApi already implements the http transport.

fixture._note: scaffolding for the quadrant comparison's own proof: performs an item deterministically with no model at all. status 'self-test' is load-bearing - quadrant/schema.json's comparable_runner_statuses excludes it, so it can never appear in a decision table, and test_quadrant.py asserts no profile assigns a role to it.

_comment: The TARGET axis (PLAN 1 L3), orthogonal to the runner axis and living in
configuration rather than code: 'Nothing in the pipeline layer knows which
quadrant it is in.'

self._note: the org works on THE REPOSITORY IT IS POINTED AT - a worktree off that repo's ref, plane leases for shared runtime, that repo's branch policy. Which repository is the VENUE's question, not this target's: in a gym run 'self' is a worktree of the arena, and in a workspace-venue smoke run it is ai-stack. The quadrant harness uses a DETACHED worktree so a comparison never leaves a branch behind.

project._note: the org pointed at an external project: agent-org's clone/workspace model, git-proxy containment, the GitHub App as the door. For a COMPARISON the workspace is a local disposable repo - a comparison must never be the first thing to touch a real target.

_comment: The runner x target comparison. PLAN 2's U4 column, QUOTED IN FULL because the
first word is the one this config used to drop:
"Gym: same anchored item run per quadrant (runner x target), outcomes
compared; stall -> oracle observed firing at least once"
'Gym:' is bound four lines above that table: "'gym' means measured runs in
`ai-orchestration-gym`, never live planes or a real target." The restatement
here previously began at 'same anchored item', so the one clause naming the
VENUE was the one clause missing from the config's own copy of the
requirement - and a four-cell comparison was then run against ai-stack and
read as satisfying the column. `venue` below is that clause, as data.
Listing the axes here rather than in code is what lets a fifth runner or a
third target be a config edit; the harness derives the matrix, and its report
always renders one row per configured cell whether or not that cell produced
a record.

_why: THE ARENA. The gym's own README: `main` is the arena holding the training
project the org iterates on, force-swapped per scenario and never built on
by hand; the harness branch holds the scenario catalog and the run ledger.
So `ref` is `main` - a run against the harness branch would be working on
the gym's tooling, not in its arena.
The path is RELATIVE and is resolved against the MAIN CHECKOUT of this repo
(the git common dir's parent), not against the caller's worktree: harness
sessions run in .claude/worktrees/wt-<id>, where '..' means something else
entirely. Override per machine with $AI_STACK_GYM_REPO or --repo.
quadrant/venue.py REFUSES this venue if it resolves to this repository.
ai-stack itself - the venue a smoke run of the HARNESS uses. It does NOT
satisfy any 'Gym:' column and quadrant/schema.json says so in the venue
kind's own rules, so selecting it cannot quietly produce evidence for U4.

quadrant._repeats_note: 1 means every cell is n=1 and the report says so in those words. Raise it to 2+ before treating any difference between quadrants as real.
quadrant._results_dir_note: NOT under .claude/. Measured 2026-08-30: a claude-code run whose workspace lived at .claude/quadrant-runs/.../workspace had every Write and Edit turned into a permission request - Claude Code treats .claude/ as a sensitive path - so the quadrant scored 1/2 on a task the model had already solved correctly in its reply. The harness would have been measuring its own directory choice.

all-cloud._desc: the default everywhere; all three roles on cloud opus

all-local._desc: no cloud calls at all; needs the inference plane healthy

local-work-cloud-review._desc: cheap production, expensive judgement - the reviewer is the last gate before a merge

cloud-work-local-test._desc: expensive production, cheap verification - useful when the test plan is mechanical

_comment: WHO passes a pipeline gate. Deliberately a SEPARATE block from `profiles`
above, not another key inside it. `profiles` is keyed by ROLE and every reader
iterates the three roles; a gate is not a role, and folding gates in would make
`resolve_role` and `describe_profile` iterate keys that are not roles. The
stronger reason is coupling: an operator switching to a cheaper MODEL profile
must not thereby also turn the human gates off. Those are two unrelated
decisions and one name must not carry both - the same reasoning that produced
`profile_locked` on the extension surface.
This block is TUNING (who passes). What a gate DOES - the state transitions,
the duty separation, the refusal of self-service - stays in queue.ps1, because
that is BEHAVIOUR. Turning a gate to `auto` is an operator decision with a real
cost: nobody looks at the work before it moves on.
Values: `human` (a person runs -ConfirmAnchor / -Approve) or `auto` (the gate
self-passes). Every auto-pass is refused unless the andon board is clear, and
every auto-pass writes an audit record under a RESERVED principal namespace
(`auto:<profile>`) that no human -By value is allowed to occupy.

attended._desc: today's behaviour, unchanged - a human confirms the anchor and releases for review

dark._desc: unattended: both gates self-pass, andon-clear, and say so in the record

_comment: THE ANDON BOARD. Conditions are DATA here and executable predicates in andon.ps1;
a condition naming a predicate that does not exist is refused, so this block cannot
declare a detector nobody implements.
Every condition here has a real incident behind it from the 2026-08-30 unattended
run - see `incident` on each. None was invented to round out a taxonomy.
`on_fire` and `on_indeterminate` are both `halt` by default and on purpose: a
condition that could not be evaluated has NOT passed. A skip that counts as a pass
is one of the failure shapes this board exists to catch.
THE ONLY TWO WORDS EITHER MAY TAKE are `halt` and `warn` (config.ps1
$script:AllowedAndonActions / config.py ALLOWED_ANDON_ACTIONS); anything else is
refused with exit 1 and no verdict, which every gate reads as `not clear`. And `warn`
does NOT buy a pass: a condition that FIRED is never a clear board, so no unattended
gate passes over one either way. It changes the board's WORD (`warned` rather than
`raised`) and the record, which is triage for a human, not permission for a machine.
Until 2026-08-30 it did buy a pass - the condition fired, the board said `clear`, the
dark gate auto-passed at exit 0 and the ledger recorded `fired=[]`, because `fired`
was derived from `action -eq halt`.
WHICH CONDITIONS MUST EXIST IS NOT DECIDED HERE. The required ids live in code
(config.ps1 $script:RequiredAndonConditions / config.py REQUIRED_ANDON_CONDITIONS),
and a board missing any of them is `incomplete`: exit 6, the ids named, no auto-pass.
Deleting an entry from the list below is therefore visible, not silent - which it was
not until 2026-08-30, when a board pruned to one of five reported `clear` with 1 of 1
evaluated and a dark gate auto-passed at exit 0. A required list kept in THIS file
would be deleted alongside the entry it names.

_ledger_note: There is no `ledger` knob here and there deliberately never was one that worked.
A raise ALWAYS goes to the gate ledger - queue.ps1 writes a decision=refused record
at the gate that halted - because a run able to switch off the record of its own
halt is the failure this whole board exists to prevent. `ledger: true` sat here
until 2026-08-30 with ZERO executable readers: the dead-knob detector shipped a dead
knob, inside its own block. `roots` below now includes `andon`, so the detector
covers this block and the next one cannot hide here.

conditions.detects: the operator's main checkout is detached, or has a rebase/merge/cherry-pick/bisect in progress
a policy knob declared in harness.config.json that no executable source reads - a setting that governs nothing while reading as though it does

params._exclude_note: GLOB patterns for what does NOT count as a reader: a test or drill that names a key exercises it rather than consuming it. config.ps1/config.py are NOT excluded - they hold the accessors, and the scan matches the DOTTED PATH, which their defaults blocks do not contain.
params._roots_note: policy KNOBS. `andon` is a root so this condition covers its OWN block - it shipped with a dead `andon.raise.ledger` in it. Named data COLLECTIONS keyed by name (profiles, gate_profiles) are not roots: they are consumed generically by a loop, so a path scan says nothing true about them. `andon.conditions` is a leaf here - the list is read whole by Get-AndonConditions - so the scan asks only whether the list itself is read, never whether each condition is. WHICH conditions are present is a different question, answered by the required-set check in andon.ps1 against config.ps1's $script:RequiredAndonConditions, not by this scan.
params._match_note: the dotted path is matched ANCHORED. Unanchored, any key that is a PREFIX of a live one reported 'read': with pipeline.gate_profile in the sources, pipeline.gate_profil, pipeline.claim_ttl and pipeline.a all passed (reproduced 2026-08-30). A container key counts as read when its own path OR any leaf beneath it is matched, which is why andon.raise is alive on the strength of andon.raise.stderr and pipeline.human_gates was not.

conditions.incident: pipeline.human_gates and runners.*.status both had zero executable readers (verified 2026-08-30); Resolve-RoleTarget had zero executable callers

conditions.detects: a function that runs git and neither inspects $LASTEXITCODE nor raises - it cannot report a git failure, so a check built on it cannot fail

params._window_note: the unit is the CALL SITE, not the function body. Asking whether a body mentioned $LASTEXITCODE anywhere gave every git call in it an amnesty from an unrelated guard clause at the top (reproduced 2026-08-30), and code OUTSIDE any function was not scanned at all - a top-level `git push | Out-Null` reported ok. A check must fall within this many lines AFTER its call to count as its check.
params._exclude_note: git-io.ps1 is the adapter that deliberately RETURNS output and leaves $LASTEXITCODE for its callers - that contract is stated in the file and is the reason callers can check at all.

conditions.detects: a work branch of this run exists on a remote - an outward action CLAUDE.md does not grant without an explicit ask
conditions.incident: DECISIONS.md 2026-08-30 'THE ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN THREE ERRORS' #3 - eleven work/* branches reached origin under an authorisation nobody gave

conditions.detects: a protected ref moved since this run recorded its baseline
conditions.incident: PLAN.md section C.2 class 4 - merging or promoting anything to main is the operator's, and no U-phase needs it

convergence._status: SPEC + NUMBER, NOT YET LIVE. Per this file's own policy-declared-unread andon rule, this block governs NOTHING until queue.ps1/config.py read it AND the reviewer charter enforces the class gate below. Wiring the reader + the severity contract is a pipeline item, not a config edit - written here as the agreed number and its derivation so the implementation has a target it cannot silently soften.
_semantics: A verification round SENDS THE ITEM BACK only on a CLASS-1 finding: it fails an acceptance criterion, is unsafe, or is wrong. CLASS-2 (correct but weaker) and CLASS-3 (cosmetic - clearer message, less-vacuous check, doc) are filed to the findings sink and NEVER hold a merge.

Convergence is a POSITIVE condition: acceptance checks pass from a clean clone with zero class-1 outstanding. It is NOT 'the refuters found nothing' - a capable refuter against a real artifact always finds SOMETHING, which is exactly why the old open-ended loop ran for tens of hours.

max_class1_rounds caps the build->refute->fix cycles that a class-1 finding may trigger. Reaching the cap with a class-1 still open is an ANDON ESCALATION to the operator, never a silent pass. Rounds that find only class-2/3 do not count against it and do not extend it - they merge and file.
convergence._derivation: Empirical, from THIS project's own runs (measured 2026-08-31). Classified every round of every multi-round item by finding severity. The LAST class-1 finding: u5 (security) at round 3 ('absence must deny', the final leak-path fix); u6dark at round 4 ('a fire that does not halt'); u4close ~round 4. Rounds 5+ everywhere were meta-verification polish - u6dark 6-7 (a check's alphabet/vacuity), u4close 8-9 (a banked check's vacuous pass, MODULE.md, a footer), u5rls round 4 (gate completeness), u8h3's 26 commits. N=2 would have CLIPPED u5's round-3 security fix; N=4+ bought only polish. So 3 - and the severity gate is what makes 3 sufficient rather than 9, because it stops polish from counting as a round at all.
convergence._per_item_override: An anchor MAY raise max_class1_rounds for genuinely high-stakes work (the personal-plane boundary is the archetype - a security item where a 4th round is cheap insurance). The default of 3 is the floor the evidence supports; raising it is a recorded anchor decision, lowering it below 2 is refused.

pipeline._note: the role -> state -> duty table stays in queue.ps1: it is behavior, not tuning. `gate_profile` names a row in `gate_profiles` above and decides WHO passes each gate. It replaced `human_gates` on 2026-08-30 (U6): that pair of booleans had zero executable readers in any language - it read as policy and governed nothing, which is exactly what the `policy-declared-unread` andon condition now refuses. THIS NOTE CALLED gate_profile THE ONLY KNOB THAT DECIDES WHETHER A HUMAN SEES A GATE, AND THAT WAS FALSE: `anchor_required: false` removes the anchor gate outright for an item created without an anchor, under ANY profile including `attended` - the item advances to ready-to-test with no anchor, no human, no gate record and no andon consultation, because a gate that is not a gate is not passed by anybody. queue.ps1 -VerifyAudit says so in words rather than counting a narrower complete. So: gate_profile decides who passes a gate; anchor_required decides whether the anchor gate exists at all.

_env_files_note: Runtime files a worktree needs but git will not materialize. The two recipe
.env files live INSIDE the OB1 submodule, so a fresh worktree clone never has
them and `docker compose -f OB1/docker/docker-compose.yml config` fails there
while passing in the main checkout - which is how the offline harness came to
fail only in worktrees. An ARRAY of lines, like _comment above: a JSON string
cannot contain a raw newline, and the first version of this note did. PowerShell
ConvertFrom-Json accepted it; Python json.loads did not - and this file has BOTH
readers (config.ps1 and config.py), so it would have broken the bridge alone.
